C0.quote: a first formal framework for long-term PB
C0.note: Participatory budgeting aggregates approval ballots into collective decisions over projects; the paper studies axiomatic and complexity aspects.

C1.quote: we investigate under which conditions these criteria can be satisfied
C1.note: Existence guarantees and impossibility results (AX) dominate. Complexity results (AL) are secondary. Fairness welfare criteria are WD-like but are coded mainly as AX.

C2.2.quote: the set of projects Aj (i) ⊆ Pj she approves of
C2.2.note: Knapsack ballots are approval sets that satisfy the budget.

C2.3.quote: agents can have personal utility functions to express their satisfaction
C2.3.note: Personal utility functions are mentioned but are private and not used in the model.

C2.4.quote: We thus need to approximate the satisfaction of an agent.
C2.4.note: Satisfaction is computed directly from the ballots. No statement is made about misreporting or sincerity.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers misreporting. Strategyproofness is mentioned only in related work.

C3.2.note: The paper never states that voters submit their held attitudes.

C4.1.quote: agreement between a voter’s ballot and the chosen projects
C4.1.note: Satisfaction is defined as cost of approved funded projects. It is described as an approximation of private utility, but the relation to utilities is not formally defined.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: we have to specify how we measure the welfare of types
C5.1.note: Satisfaction, relative satisfaction and share are used in the results as welfare and proportionality criteria.

C5.2.quote: sat m j (I, πj , i) = c(πj ∩ Aj (i))
C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated directly on ballots. No statement relates ballots to held attitudes, though satisfaction is called an approximation.

VOT.note: Agents only provide fixed approval ballots and take no modelled action.

ORG.note: The municipality's choice of allocation is the rule's output, not a modelled agent.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two types are present.

claims.quote: disregards the possibility of achieving fair outcomes over time
taking the long-term viewpoint allows us to approximate forms of fairness
these outcomes are not particularly fair with respects to the two districts

C9.1.note: Claims concern fairness towards voter types and the benefit of long-term PB.

C9.2.quote: We thus need to approximate the satisfaction of an agent.
C9.2.note: Fairness towards voters from ballot-based satisfaction needs an assumption that ballots reflect held attitudes or welfare. This is not stated, and no strategic behaviour assumption is given.

C10.1.note: No explicit procedural reading is stated.
